$comment: Licensing: FDC is a work of the US federal government and is in the PUBLIC
DOMAIN. We may store it, serve it and redistribute it. That is a real
contrast with Open Food Facts, which is ODbL and carries share-alike duties
Each entry is pinned by URL AND sha256. FDC filenames carry a release date
and the files behind them are replaced, so an unpinned download would
silently change the corpus under you. A checksum mismatch is a hard failure,
not a warning: quietly ingesting a different release is how nutrition data
To move to a newer release: find it at
re-run. Nutrients are matched by nutrient_nbr, not by surrogate id, so a new
release does not need code changes.
